title: Can Broad Biomedical Knowledge be Contextualized into Scenario-Grounded Propositions?
abstract: arXiv:2605.27082v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Biomedical discovery often requires connecting broad biomedical knowledge with specific experimental or clinical data. Background knowledge suggests relevant mechanisms but is usually too general to map directly onto dataset variables, while data-driven patterns can be dataset-specific and hard to interpret mechanistically. We study this missing link as knowledge contextualization: transforming broad biomedical knowledge into evidence-supported, scenario-grounded propositions that domain experts can inspect, replay, and validate. We propose SCENE, a bi-level multi-agent framework that treats knowledge contextualization as iterative search. The upper level converts broad knowledge into search directions and grounds them in the dataset schema. The lower level executes these directions through multi-objective optimization to identify concrete propositions that balance evidential strength and data support. Feedback between the two levels

translated_title: 广泛的生物医学知识能否被情境化为基于具体场景的命题？
translated_abstract: 生物医学发现通常需要将广泛的生物医学知识与具体的实验或临床数据相联系。背景知识能够提示相关机制，但通常过于宽泛，难以直接映射到数据集变量上；而数据驱动的模式往往局限于特定数据集，且难以从机制角度加以解释。我们将这一缺失的环节研究为“知识情境化”：即将广泛的生物医学知识转化为有证据支持的、基于具体场景的命题，使领域专家能够对其进行检查、回放和验证。我们提出了SCENE，一个双层多智能体框架，将知识情境化视为迭代搜索过程。上层将广泛的知识转化为搜索方向，并将其落实到数据集模式中；下层通过多目标优化执行这些方向，以识别在证据强度和数据支持之间取得平衡的具体命题。两层之间的反馈……
tldr: 提出了SCENE——一个双层多智能体框架，将知识情境化建模为迭代搜索过程，把广泛的生物医学知识转化为有证据支持、基于具体场景的命题，从而弥合背景知识与具体数据之间的鸿沟。
en_tdlr: SCENE, a bi-level multi-agent framework, treats knowledge contextualization as iterative search, transforming broad biomedical knowledge into evidence-supported, scenario-grounded propositions to bridge general background knowledge with dataset-specific evidence.
